contexts.finding: Sox2-labeled populations show expandable culture potential and neuronal, astroglial or Sox2-retaining phenotypes in distinct assays. Sparse mixed clusters support conditional common-founder and self-renewal interpretations. Running comparisons report increased cycle-related markers and nonsignificant GFP-density differences, but reporter-control identity is unresolved. Complete lineage cycles and population-maintenance mechanisms remain hypotheses.
limitations: The 5.5-kb Sox2-promoter GFP transgenic line 1F7 is distinct from the 3.1-kb Sox2-GFP/Cre viral cassette and ROSA26 GFP or beta-gal reporters. Initial histology uses six-week mice; supplementary IHC specifies six to nine weeks, whereas clonal tracing uses six-week to three-month ROSA26 mice. Sex and a complete assay-specific animal manifest are not reported.

Marker meaning depends on niche and morphology. SGZ radial processes express nestin, GFAP and BLBP; lack of somatic signal makes nonradial nestin/GFAP assessment infeasible, not a demonstrated negative phenotype. Hilar astrocytic and SVZ ependymal marker combinations cannot be assigned the SGZ stem-cell interpretation automatically.

FGF2/EGF growth conditions and FACS select an expandable culture population. The preparation pools four pairs of hippocampi; the complete independent culture/animal allocation is unavailable. Enrichment and serial passage do not measure in vivo self-renewal frequency or establish that every cultured cell preserves its original in vivo potential.

The seven-day 5-micromolar forskolin assay shows neuronal and astrocytic markers. RIP-positive oligodendroglial differentiation uses a separate coculture with P0 rat hippocampal neurons and a donor beta-gal label. These conditions do not show in vivo tripotency, functional myelination or all three fates and serial renewal in one fully documented founder lineage.

At seven days, the lentiviral control reports SOX2 in 70% of GFP-positive cells and NeuN-positive off-target labeling of 26 +/- 3%, with n=800 cells, not 800 animals. BrdU selection is used to exclude nondividing off-target neurons. Animal-level denominators, initial recombination timing and complete lineage specificity are not established by this endpoint control.

Population fate mapping uses 100 mg/kg BrdU daily for seven days, starting ten or twenty-eight days after lentivirus. Methods specifies collection four weeks after the last injection, while Figure 3A marks analyses at days thirty-eight and fifty-eight. These statements do not reconcile to one exact label-age schedule; the injection route is unspecified.

Table 1 uses separate immunostaining panels, so marker percentages are not a partition of one cohort. Its S-100beta row prints three positive cells among thirty-two and 6.1%; these disagree because 3/32 is 9.375%. Neither value is silently substituted, and exact pooled fate probabilities are not admitted.

Retroviral specificity is reported as 92 +/- 1.7% SOX2 colabeling at seven days in a separate n=3 control. Twenty-one-day lineage assignments rely on sparse labeling and proximity, without founder barcodes, live division trees or a reported chance-collision bound. Clusters and hemispheres are nested within twenty-seven animals.

Table 2 lists 301 neuron-only, seven astrocyte-only, ten Sox2-only, fifteen Sox2-plus-neuron, one neuron-plus-astrocyte and twenty-nine undetermined clusters, totaling 363 across fifty-four hemispheres. Homogeneous categories include one- and two-cell clusters. These are cluster counts, not independent animal counts or an unbiased lineage-fate probability distribution.

Figure S4 traverses optical depth in micrometres, not elapsed time. The radial-process example is a fixed mixed cluster, not observation of its founder or a conversion event. Figure 4D has differing GFP and beta-gal panel labels; reporter identity needs clarification before panel-specific quantitative reuse.

Running Methods specifies seven transgenic runners and seven wild-type littermate controls, but Figure 5 shows and counts GFP-positive cells in both groups. The main paper and supplement do not resolve this control-genotype conflict. A matched reporter-genotype intervention effect is therefore not admitted.

The comparison uses individual cages with or without wheel access, seven daily 100 mg/kg BrdU injections and collection twenty-four hours after the last injection; the route is unreported. Figure 5A and caption do not uniquely fix wheel-access duration. Accumulated BrdU, terminal Ki67 and DCX are different readouts, not completed neuron production or functional integration.

Figure 5 reports densities per million cubic micrometres. GFP is sampled across the dentate rostrocaudal axis, while other markers use four dorsal hippocampal sections. Supplementary histology uses forty-micrometre sections; the stated every-twelfth-section and 440-micrometre interval lack a spacing-reference convention. GFP counting is described as blind; full animal allocation, raw measurements and multiplicity-adjusted analyses are unavailable.

Reported GFP-density comparisons have P=0.1724, n=7 for total reporter cells and P=0.1125, n=5 for radial cells. These nonsignificant comparisons do not establish equivalence, conservation of whole-population counts or a constant pool through time. The control-genotype conflict also applies to these nulls.

Figure 6 models population maintenance and possible radial/nonradial lineage relations. Its caption explicitly distinguishes asymmetric contribution at population level from asymmetric division of individual cells. Birth, death, survival, marker kinetics and a regulated feedback variable are not jointly measured; no universal stem-cell minimum or closed homeostatic construction is established.

All main scientific text, methods, six figures, two tables and the complete fourteen-page supplement were reviewed. Raw images, animal-level records and custom analysis code were not independently reproduced.

contexts.finding: Sox2-labeled populations show expandable culture potential and neuronal, astroglial or Sox2-retaining phenotypes in distinct assays. Sparse mixed clusters support conditional common-founder and self-renewal interpretations. Running comparisons report increased cycle-related markers and nonsignificant GFP-density differences, but reporter-control identity is unresolved. Complete lineage cycles and population-maintenance mechanisms remain hypotheses.
limitations: The 5.5-kb Sox2-promoter GFP transgenic line 1F7 is distinct from the 3.1-kb Sox2-GFP/Cre viral cassette and ROSA26 GFP or beta-gal reporters. Initial histology uses six-week mice; supplementary IHC specifies six to nine weeks, whereas clonal tracing uses six-week to three-month ROSA26 mice. Sex and a complete assay-specific animal manifest are not reported.

Marker meaning depends on niche and morphology. SGZ radial processes express nestin, GFAP and BLBP; lack of somatic signal makes nonradial nestin/GFAP assessment infeasible, not a demonstrated negative phenotype. Hilar astrocytic and SVZ ependymal marker combinations cannot be assigned the SGZ stem-cell interpretation automatically.

FGF2/EGF growth conditions and FACS select an expandable culture population. The preparation pools four pairs of hippocampi; the complete independent culture/animal allocation is unavailable. Enrichment and serial passage do not measure in vivo self-renewal frequency or establish that every cultured cell preserves its original in vivo potential.

The seven-day 5-micromolar forskolin assay shows neuronal and astrocytic markers. RIP-positive oligodendroglial differentiation uses a separate coculture with P0 rat hippocampal neurons and a donor beta-gal label. These conditions do not show in vivo tripotency, functional myelination or all three fates and serial renewal in one fully documented founder lineage.

At seven days, the lentiviral control reports SOX2 in 70% of GFP-positive cells and NeuN-positive off-target labeling of 26 +/- 3%, with n=800 cells, not 800 animals. BrdU selection is used to exclude nondividing off-target neurons. Animal-level denominators, initial recombination timing and complete lineage specificity are not established by this endpoint control.

Population fate mapping uses 100 mg/kg BrdU daily for seven days, starting ten or twenty-eight days after lentivirus. Methods specifies collection four weeks after the last injection, while Figure 3A marks analyses at days thirty-eight and fifty-eight. These statements do not reconcile to one exact label-age schedule; the injection route is unspecified.

Table 1 uses separate immunostaining panels, so marker percentages are not a partition of one cohort. Its S-100beta row prints three positive cells among thirty-two and 6.1%; these disagree because 3/32 is 9.375%. Neither value is silently substituted, and exact pooled fate probabilities are not admitted.

Retroviral specificity is reported as 92 +/- 1.7% SOX2 colabeling at seven days in a separate n=3 control. Twenty-one-day lineage assignments rely on sparse labeling and proximity, without founder barcodes, live division trees or a reported chance-collision bound. Clusters and hemispheres are nested within twenty-seven animals.

Table 2 lists 301 neuron-only, seven astrocyte-only, ten Sox2-only, fifteen Sox2-plus-neuron, one neuron-plus-astrocyte and twenty-nine undetermined clusters, totaling 363 across fifty-four hemispheres. Homogeneous categories include one- and two-cell clusters. These are cluster counts, not independent animal counts or an unbiased lineage-fate probability distribution.

Figure S4 traverses optical depth in micrometres, not elapsed time. The radial-process example is a fixed mixed cluster, not observation of its founder or a conversion event. Figure 4D has differing GFP and beta-gal panel labels; reporter identity needs clarification before panel-specific quantitative reuse.

Running Methods specifies seven transgenic runners and seven wild-type littermate controls, but Figure 5 shows and counts GFP-positive cells in both groups. The main paper and supplement do not resolve this control-genotype conflict. A matched reporter-genotype intervention effect is therefore not admitted.

The comparison uses individual cages with or without wheel access, seven daily 100 mg/kg BrdU injections and collection twenty-four hours after the last injection; the route is unreported. Figure 5A and caption do not uniquely fix wheel-access duration. Accumulated BrdU, terminal Ki67 and DCX are different readouts, not completed neuron production or functional integration.

Figure 5 reports densities per million cubic micrometres. GFP is sampled across the dentate rostrocaudal axis, while other markers use four dorsal hippocampal sections. Supplementary histology uses forty-micrometre sections; the stated every-twelfth-section and 440-micrometre interval lack a spacing-reference convention. GFP counting is described as blind; full animal allocation, raw measurements and multiplicity-adjusted analyses are unavailable.

Reported GFP-density comparisons have P=0.1724, n=7 for total reporter cells and P=0.1125, n=5 for radial cells. These nonsignificant comparisons do not establish equivalence, conservation of whole-population counts or a constant pool through time. The control-genotype conflict also applies to these nulls.

Figure 6 models population maintenance and possible radial/nonradial lineage relations. Its caption explicitly distinguishes asymmetric contribution at population level from asymmetric division of individual cells. Birth, death, survival, marker kinetics and a regulated feedback variable are not jointly measured; no universal stem-cell minimum or closed homeostatic construction is established.

All main scientific text, methods, six figures, two tables and the complete fourteen-page supplement were reviewed. Raw images, animal-level records and custom analysis code were not independently reproduced.
